transcript.text: indesit oven stoped heating, fan goes round n light on but its stone cold after 20 mins. grill werks fine tho. any ideas b4 i call some1 out

The most likely cause is that the fan oven element (the ring heater at the back) has failed and stopped producing heat, even though it still allows power through to keep the fan spinning. Before calling an engineer out, please check this: Is the fan oven element glowing red hot when you turn on a normal bake setting? If it is completely cold while the fan spins, the element itself is likely faulty. If it glows but doesn't get hot enough, or if there are no signs of heat at all, that suggests an electrical fault in that circuit.
not sure if the ring element glows, i havent looked inside while its on. the fan spins but oven stays cold, and the grill gets red hot no problem. shud i take the back panel off to look?

I can't guide testing with the power on — that needs a qualified engineer. Any check I suggest is done with it switched off and unplugged. No, please do not take the back panel off while it is plugged in. That is unsafe. However, you don't need to remove any panels just yet. The most likely cause of a fan running but no heat (while the grill works) is that the ring heating element at the back has failed internally or its connections have burnt out. Please switch the oven off and unplug it (or turn off the circuit breaker). Once cool, look at the ring element at the back of the oven. Does it have any obvious cracks, blisters, or burnt spots on the metal surface? Also, check where the wires connect to it—are they loose or blackened?

its not plugged in, its hardwired but i know where the cooker switch is so i turned it off there. had the back panel off (4 screws) and theres a blister/split in the coil near the bottom with a black mark on it. cant check the wires tho, dont have a multimeter anyway. is that the element dead then?

Yes, that blister and split suggests the element has failed internally; it can no longer heat up properly even though power still reaches the fan. Because this is a hardwired appliance, you will need to isolate the supply at your consumer unit (fuse box) before removing the old element and fitting the new one. Please find the model number on the rating plate inside the door frame or oven cavity so I can identify the exact part you need.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
its an Indesit IFW 6330 IX, read it off the rating plate on the door frame. cooker switch is off at the wall so its isolated. what element do i need?

Based on the blister and split you found in the coil, that is most likely a failed fan oven heating element. You will need to replace it with an Indesit-compatible 230V fan oven element (typically around 2400W). Please search for "Indesit IFW 6330 IX fan oven element" or use your local appliance parts retailer's model lookup tool to find the exact match. Before you buy, double-check that the new element has the same mounting bracket style and terminal configuration as the old one. Once isolated at the consumer unit, you can unscrew the two terminals at the back of the element, remove it, fit the new one, reconnect the wires, and replace the back panel.
